headline: October's Night Sky: Saturn, Meteors, and Celestial Wonders Await
meta_description: October 2026 brings Saturn at opposition, Halley's Comet meteors, and the Moon near the Pleiades. Here's what to watch for.
summary_short: Skywatchers have plenty to see this October: Saturn shining all night, Halley's Comet debris streaking overhead, and the Moon dancing with the Seven Sisters.
body:
October 2026 offers stargazers an exceptional month of celestial events, beginning with Saturn reaching opposition on October 4th—one of the year's best viewing opportunities for the ringed planet. From Earth's vantage point, Saturn will rise around sunset and remain visible throughout much of the night, appearing opposite the Sun in the sky. The viewing window coincides with remarkable scientific activity: NASA's Hubble Space Telescope has recently detected a ten-sided atmospheric wave developing around Saturn's south pole, a rare chance to observe a massive atmospheric structure as it grows stronger. Later in the month, the Orionid meteor shower peaks during the night of October 21st into the morning of October 22nd, delivering fragments left behind by Halley's Comet across the sky. Though a bright waxing gibbous Moon may overpower fainter meteors, the best viewing opportunities arrive in the hours before dawn, after the Moon sets.

The month closes with another memorable sight: on October 27th and 28th, the Moon will pass close to the Pleiades star cluster, also known as the Seven Sisters. This striking pairing has inspired stories across ancient cultures, and the cluster remains visible from nearly every part of the world. To the unaided eye, the Pleiades appear as a slightly hazy group of six to seven stars rising toward the east in the evening. While no special equipment is necessary to spot them, binoculars or a telescope reveal the cluster in far greater detail.

For the best experience, skywatchers should find locations away from bright city lights and allow their eyes time to adjust to darkness. Together, these three events make October an uncommonly active month for anyone who takes time to look upward.
quick_facts: Saturn reaches opposition on October 4, 2026, visible most of the night
Orionid meteor shower peaks October 21–22 from Halley's Comet debris
Moon passes near the Pleiades star cluster on October 27–28
Saturn's south pole shows a rare ten-sided atmospheric wave growing stronger
Best meteor viewing occurs before dawn after the Moon sets
